newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - July 21.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - July 21.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the South African press on Monday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
BUSINESS DAY

- The Inkatha Freedom Party (IFP) national conference set five preconditions on Sunday for reconciliation with the African National Congress and warned that the killing of IFP leaders was an obstacle to securing a peace settlement.
- Gauteng's premiership battle took a new turn on Sunday as the African National Congress-led tripartite alliance backed provincial health minister Amos Masondo for premier.

- The Congress of South African Trade Unions' (Cosatu) investment companies and three affiliates have become major shareholders in hospital management company Network Healthcare Holdings (Netcare) NTC.J.
- New York, London and other global share markets could experience a nervous week following an unexpected slide on Friday which saw the Dow Jones index fall 130 points to 7 891, dealers said.

- Gauteng had at least 108 organised crime syndicates and serious corruption existed within its criminal justice system, provincial police management and the safety and security department told Deputy President Thabo Mbeki at the weekend.
BUSINESS REPORT
- Union investment companies and an organisation of black doctors will take a 200 million rand stake in Netcare's 920 million rand acquisition of Clinic Holdings, which was announced at the weekend.
- Labour Minister Tito Mboweni said last week he would quit his post next year.

- Worldwide African Investment Holdings, the black economic empowerment group, came in from the cold to acquire control of the 1,4 billion rand lion-a-year Zenex Oil, the petrol retailer, in a 400 million rand deal, sources said at the weekend.
- Housing Minister Sankie Mthembi-Mahanyele said at the weekend that she and provincial housing MEC's have agreed to allocate 220,000 subsidies worth 4,2 billion rand this financial year.
- A bonanza is ahead for Towles, Edgar Jacobs (Tej) shareholders who stayed on for the ride after the acquisition of a controlling stake in the clothing company by a Johannesburg consortium.
SAKE BEELD
- The strike of thousands of sugar industry workers which paralysed the industry since July 2 is over.
- The gold price this weekend continued to build on its good display on Friday in London.
- Worldwide African Investment Holdings (WAIH) on Friday acquired a controlling stake in Zenex Oil for 400 million rand.
THE STAR

- Hundreds of false motor vehicle clearance certificates have been detected at Johannesburg's traffic licensing department over the past two months, but many more are going unchecked in Greater Johannesburg because manpower is not available to deal with the problem.
- A burning cigarette butt tossed in the dry grass outside FNB Stadium on Saturday may have sparked the fire which gutted five minibuses and five cars during the Iwisa Charity Spectacular.
- Max, the Johannesburg zoo gorilla who brought a suspected criminal to book last week, was recuperating well.
- The Inkatha Freedom Party has called on the government to scrap the Truth and Reconciliation Commission because the commission had failed in its purpose to foster reconciliation.

- An armaments manufacturer, Denel, has laid charges against The Sunday Independent, The Star's sister publication, for disclosing details of a sensitive seven billion rand weapons export deal to an unnamed Middle Eastern country.
